pages.text: A seed touches the melt and is drawn up at speed v: the melt freezes onto it, releasing its latent heat into the crystal. The heater's superheat sets the temperature gradient G at the growth front, and v/G decides what the crystal keeps - too fast, and it traps vacancies; too slow, interstitials; near the critical ratio, neither (Voronkov). An impurity is taken in only k_eff as readily as it sits in the melt; pulling slowly and stirring hard brings k_eff down to its equilibrium value (Burton-Prim-Slichter).
$(thing)Set$(): Heater temperature, Pull rate v, Rotation ω.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Convection in the melt: the superheat varies by ±2%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): The melt has frozen: the heaters are below its melting point; The melt is so hot it attacks the crucible and boils off; The iridium crucible softens above 2,800 K.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The faster it is pulled, the sooner the boule is done.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Superheat: ΔT = T − T_m$(br)Gradient at the front: G ≈ G₀ + ΔT/L$(br)Voronkov ratio v/G: ξ = v/G$(br)Boundary layer: δ ∝ ω^(−1/2)$(br)Effective segregation k_eff: k_eff = k₀/(k₀ + (1 − k₀)e^(−vδ/D))$(br)Crystal purity: purity = 1 − k_eff·c₀
